criterion_as_frozen: On chase_to_goal, at least 9 of 10 seeds reach accuracy >= 0.99; AND on chase_to_goal_weighted, at least 8 of 10 seeds reach accuracy >= 0.99; AND the mean step count over successful runs stays within 0.25 of Q3's 4.54.
what_actually_happened: The intervention did exactly half of what was predicted, and the half it did was the useless
half. Q3's collapse mode is GONE: no Q4 run lands below 0.6322, where four of ten Q3 runs sat
between 0.4181 and 0.5105. The bimodality is genuinely cured -- all twenty Q4 runs fall in the
But the good mode is gone with it. Q3 reached 0.9994-1.0000 on six of ten seeds; Q4's best run
anywhere is 0.9500 and its best on chase_to_goal is 0.9050. Grounding the state removed the
variance by pulling both tails to the middle.
why_the_hypothesis_was_wrong: The hypothesis said Q3 fails because the state does not track position, so supplying position
would let the arrival head do its job. Q4 shows the state can be made to track position and
the arrival head still does not reach 0.99. Position information is therefore not the binding
The likely reason -- proposed here as an explanation, not established -- is that a 24-way
cross-entropy at every one of eight steps dominates the single scalar arrival signal, so the
state is optimised to name the node rather than to make the one binary decision that matters.
The auxiliary task is easier than the real task and absorbs the representation. That is a
generic hazard of auxiliary supervision, not a fact about halting.
programme_consequence: No second variant is issued. The kill condition frozen in advance says the mechanism
hypothesis is false and Q-Neuro 3.0 cycle 1 closes with Q3 recorded as an unreliable
architecture rather than a compute-saving one.
